ai.title: Remove Freebuff waiting-room queued state from session lifecycle
ai.summary: The Freebuff free-tier no longer has a queued state: picking a model POSTs straight to an active session instead of joining a per-model queue. The `queued` branch is deleted from the `FreebuffSessionServerResponse` union in `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`, and the CLI's `nextDelayMs`, `getFreebuffInstanceId`, `shouldReleaseSlot`, `apply`, and startup-takeover logic in `cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts` no longer handle it. `cli/src/app.tsx`'s `AuthedSurface` routes only `none` and terminal statuses through the waiting room, while `cli/src/components/waiting-room-screen.tsx` drops the queued position panel and its `formatWait`/`formatElapsed` helpers. The `committedModelId` in `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx` is now always `null`, and `useNow` in the waiting room ticks once a minute (not per-second) since the queue timer no longer exists. A secondary change removes the disabled server status and `queueDepthByModel`, collapsing the landing response to quota and referral snapshots only.
ai.evidence: Removed the `queued` session status from the FreebuffSessionServerResponse union and all CLI handling in cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts (nextDelayMs, getFreebuffInstanceId, shouldReleaseSlot, apply, startup-takeover branch, and the landing GET), cli/src/app.tsx (AuthedSurface routing in AuthedSurface), cli/src/components/waiting-room-screen.tsx (removed queued position panel, formatWait/formatElapsed, and isQueued gating), cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx (committedModelId no longer reads session.status === 'queued'), and common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts (deleted the queued union member, the disabled status, and queueDepthByModel from none).
ai.unknowns: The diff is client-side only; it does not show the server-side removal of queueing or whether the `x-freebuff-model` header now means 'model to admit' rather than 'model to queue for'.

changes.what: Removed the `{ status: 'queued', ... }` and `{ status: 'disabled' }` union members from `FreebuffSessionServerResponse` and dropped `queueDepthByModel` from the `none` status, leaving quota and referral snapshots as the only pre-join metadata.

Deleted all `queued` handling from `nextDelayMs`, `getFreebuffInstanceId`, `shouldReleaseSlot`, `apply`, the startup-takeover branch, and the landing GET; changed `POLL_INTERVAL_QUEUED_MS` removal and the admission bell to fire on `none` to `active`; set `committedModelId` to always null.
Removed `session.status === 'queued'` from the `AuthedSurface` waiting-room routing condition so only `none` and terminal statuses route through the pre-chat screen.

Removed the `isQueued` branch, the queued position panel (`queuedTitleText`, `session.position`/`queueDepth` display), and the `formatWait`/`formatElapsed` helpers; changed `useNow` from per-second to once-a-minute ticking on landing.
Set `committedModelId` to a `null` literal constant since the queued state no longer exists, and updated the doc comment to say the POST admits straight to active.

ai.title: Add waitForBootSignal to e2e session utils
ai.summary: Added `waitForBootSignal` method to `FreebuffSession` class and exported `FREEBUFF_BOOT_SIGNALS` constant. Replaces reliance on single ASCII logo detection with polling against multiple static strings (e.g., 'Start coding for free', 'Pick a model to start') to handle CI runner variability where full ASCII art may not render. Changes scoped to `freebuff/e2e/utils/freebuff-session.ts` and `freebuff/e2e/utils/index.ts`. Method polls every 500ms up to 30s timeout, throwing error with last output snapshot on failure.

eli5.text: When you open the assistant in a fresh terminal, the automated checks that confirm it started correctly now look for a broader set of on-screen prompts (like 'Start coding for free' or 'Pick a model to start') instead of relying solely on the ASCII logo, so the check works reliably across different terminal setups used in continuous integration. The change is live today in the end-to-end test utilities used by developers building the free-tier session flow.

ai.title: Add chat title generation analytics event
ai.summary: Added FREEBUFF_CHAT_TITLE_GENERATED to AnalyticsEvent enum in common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts. Tracks server-side new-thread title generation attempts with outcome (generated|empty|unknown_model|error|aborted), latencyMs, model, and titleLength properties. Enables queryable failure/fallback rates and added latency metrics.

eli5.text: When you start a new chat, the system generates a title for it, and now it records how that title was created. Every attempt to make a title is tracked with details like whether it succeeded or failed, what tool made it, how long it took, and how long the title ended up being. If you looked at the analytics dashboard, you'd see a new category of data showing how often titles are being generated automatically versus when they fail or come back empty, along with timing information for each try.

facts: OSC 52 caps its base64 payload at 32 KB (clipboard.ts OSC52_MAX_PAYLOAD). base64 is ~4/3 of the raw byte count, so the raw-text ceiling is ~24 KB. Leave headroom for tmux/screen passthrough wrapping and the message framing.

Return the longest suffix of `s` that fits in `maxBytes`, cut on a UTF-8 codepoint boundary (and a line boundary when one is close by) so the result is valid text. Used as the last-resort fallback when dropping tool bodies still can't get the transcript under the clipboard budget.
Prefer cutting at the next line boundary if it's nearby, for cleaner output.
Avoid breaking out of the fence if the content itself contains ```.

Tool results are stored as strings; many are a JSON envelope (e.g. the `[{"type":"json","value":{...}}]` shape from terminal/tool calls). Pretty-print when the string parses as JSON so the transcript is readable; otherwise keep the raw text. Returns the fence language to use alongside the body.
entries.title: New slash command /copy
entries.summary: New slash commands: `/copy`. New files: `cli/src/commands/copy-conversation.ts`.

ai.title: /copy serializes conversation to clipboard
ai.summary: Added a `/copy` slash command (aliases `/copy-chat` and `/export`) that serializes the full conversation - user text, assistant text, reasoning blocks, tool calls with inputs and outputs, and sub-agents - into Markdown and writes it to the system clipboard. Over SSH the OSC 52 payload caps at 32 KB (`OSC52_TEXT_BUDGET_BYTES = 22_000`), so `serializeConversation` progressively drops the largest tool results then tool inputs, replacing them with omission notes, and falls back to hard truncation via `keepTailBytes` when the remaining content still exceeds the budget; local sessions use pbcopy/xclip with no size cap and always copy the full transcript.
ai.evidence: New file `cli/src/commands/copy-conversation.ts` defines `serializeConversation`, `SerializedConversation`, and `handleCopyConversationCommand`; the `copy` command is registered in `cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts` with aliases `['copy-chat', 'export']` and added to `cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts` with description 'Copy the full conversation (messages + tool results) to the clipboard'.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not reveal how `copyTextToClipboard`, `isRemoteSession`, or `showClipboardMessage` in `cli/src/utils/clipboard` are implemented or whether the OSC 52 path is exercised on all remote sessions.

ai.title: Add referral lifecycle analytics events
ai.summary: Added `FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_REDEEMED`, `FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_COMPLETED`, and `FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_SWEEP` to the `AnalyticsEvent` enum in `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`. These events track the referral program server lifecycle, emitted from `packages/billing` via the server logger to Axiom. The `sweep` event aggregates outcomes across the pending population once per run to avoid high-volume per-evaluation ingestion.

eli5.text: The product now records three new milestones for its referral program: when someone uses a referral, when that referral finishes converting, and a daily snapshot of all the referrals still waiting to finish. These events are collected through the billing system and sent to the analytics store, with the snapshot event summarizing results across the entire pending list in a single report rather than logging each referral one by one. This is live today as part of the referral program server logic.

entries.title: CLI update: index
entries.summary: New files: `cli/src/utils/engagement.ts`, `common/src/util/engagement-tracker.ts`.

ai.title: CLI free-tier engaged-time heartbeat via shared EngagementTracker
ai.summary: Adds a Freebuff-only engaged-time heartbeat in the CLI, reusing `./activity-tracker` as the presence signal and emitting one `PRODUCT_ACTIVE_MINUTE` per active minute with `surface` set to `cli` (no tab/visibility concept in a terminal, so idleness alone gates the count). The tracking lives in a new shared `EngagementTracker` in `common/src/util/engagement-tracker.ts` that fires every `ENGAGEMENT_INTERVAL_MS` (1 minute) and skips ticks where the user has been idle past `ENGAGEMENT_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` (5 minutes); the CLI wraps its timers with `.unref()` so the heartbeat never keeps the process alive on exit, and `exitFreebuffCleanly()` stops it before flushing analytics. `PRODUCT_ACTIVE_MINUTE` is added to `AnalyticsEvent` and to `ALWAYS_TRACK_EVENTS` (never sampled), and `product_active_minute` is placed on the Axiom denylist so PostHog remains the system of record for this high-volume metric. This is the most user-relevant of several changes: two new modules, the engine wiring in `index.tsx`, exit cleanup in `exitFreebuffCleanly`, one new enum entry, sampling guard, and the Axiom denylist; tests cover tick/visibility/idle/idempotency behavior.
ai.evidence: New files `cli/src/utils/engagement.ts` and `common/src/util/engagement-tracker.ts`; `cli/src/index.tsx` calls `startEngagementTracking()` after renderer creation gated on `IS_FREEBUFF`; `cli/src/utils/freebuff-exit.ts` calls `stopEngagementTracking()` before flushing analytics in `exitFreebuffCleanly()`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the web/desktop shell consuming `EngagementTracker` yet, even though the module doc describes browser and desktop wiring.

changes.what: CLI heartbeat that starts an `EngagementTracker` emitting `PRODUCT_ACTIVE_MINUTE` with `surface: 'cli'`, driven by `./activity-tracker`'s activity signal and unref'd timers.
Framework-agnostic `EngagementTracker` class plus `ENGAGEMENT_INTERVAL_MS` (60_000) and `ENGAGEMENT_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` (300_000), with injectable `emit`, clock, and scheduler for tests.
Imports and calls `startEngagementTracking()` only when `IS_FREEBUFF` is true, after `createCliRenderer` and before rendering the app.
Calls `stopEngagementTracking()` at the start of `exitFreebuffCleanly()` so no engaged-minute fires mid-teardown before analytics flush.
Adds the `PRODUCT_ACTIVE_MINUTE` enum entry with documentation tying it to per-minute event counting and the `engagement-tracker` module.
Adds `AnalyticsEvent.PRODUCT_ACTIVE_MINUTE` to `ALWAYS_TRACK_EVENTS` so engaged-time minutes are never sampled.
